question: to the Commission Jessica Polfjärd (PPE) Subject:

Both the Industrial Accelerator Act and the proposed revision of the CO2 standards for cars and vans refer to ‘low-carbon steel’ without defining it. In both cases, the definition is left to future delegated acts under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation. 1.
Will the Commission ensure a single, coordinated definition of low-carbon steel for both laws, and, if so, by when?
How will the Commission avoid the application of two different definitions at the same time?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) Article 14 of the proposal for the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA)1 ensures the necessary coherence between the CO2 standards provisions and the IAA provisions on public procurement and incentives concerning the low carbon definition. For both purposes, a single definition of low-carbon steel will be developed by the Commission in a delegated act on iron and steel products under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation2, currently foreseen for the second quarter of 2027. The Commission is aware of the need to prevent legal uncertainty and market fragmentation that could result from parallel or divergent definitions. This will be avoided by adopting a single definition of low carbon steel in the said delegated act under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation.
